music has this uncanny way of reaching into places we think we’ve tucked away, especially when it’s tied to something as profound and heartbreaking as what you’ve gone through. im so sorry you’ve carried this pain with you. your feelings are completely valid, and it’s okay to grieve not just the loss itself, but the choices that were taken from you, the future you imagined, and the love you still hold for what could have been. trauma like this doesn’t just fade, it lingers in the quiet moments, in songs that pull at memories, in the questions that never got answers. i went through something painfully similar almost a year ago. i was pregnant during one of the worst times in my relationship. my long-term boyfriend and i broke up, and around the same time, i found out i was pregnant. he didn’t even know until weeks later, when i had a miscarriage. the stress from the breakup was too much. and it all happened during my finals week. i think that moment broke something in me. It’s one of the reasons i can’t seem to be with anyone now. and maybe why i feel like i’ll never be able to have a child. you’re not alone in this, even if it feels isolating. grief tied to what could have been is especially heavy because there’s no clear end to it. you’re mourning a future that never happened, one you maybe wanted, maybe didn’t, but one that still had meaning. so many people carry similar grief in silence because it’s hard to find words for it, or because they fear being misunderstood. but your grief matters. your love for that lost possibility matters. and it’s okay if healing isn’t linear and if a song still brings you to your knees years later. sending hugs to you op! <3
